segments.label: Operator of an ad- or content-supported website
Owner-operator of a small business website with no security staff
Platform / reliability engineering team at a mid-market software company
IT / security engineer responsible for workforce and machine access to internal applications
Low-evidence probe segment: small team considering running code close to users

roles.label: IT / security engineer for workforce access

approved_jobs.statement: When automated clients consume a site's content at a scale that raises hosting cost without returning readers, help the site operator regain control over which automated clients may access the content while keeping human and search discoverability intact.
When a business-critical website is unreachable under a flood of requests, help an operator without security staff restore availability now and stop it recurring.
When content delivery, egress and bandwidth become a leading infrastructure cost, help the responsible engineer or operator reduce that cost without breaking dynamic and API traffic.

When selecting or re-selecting a provider to sit in front of a web property, help the responsible team compare candidates against reliability history, dynamic-traffic support, billing predictability and compliance evidence before committing.
When a single upstream provider's failure takes an entire stack offline, help the architecture owner find and reduce that dependency without duplicating every system.

When remote staff, contractors and automated build systems still reach internal applications through a legacy VPN, help the IT or security engineer provide per-request verified access without requiring a persistent client on every machine.
When a security team must run a formal evaluation of converged network-security services, help them write criteria that separate natively built capability from third-party-integrated capability.
When an existing customer hits a support delay or discovers a needed capability is gated to a higher tier, help them resolve the issue or decide whether to change plan or provider.
When a platform-level default is about to change what automated clients may do on monetised pages, help a site owner work out what changes for them and what to decide before the effective date.
approved_jobs.dated_context: An industry default change takes effect 2026-09-15 and applies automatically to new accounts, new sites and existing free-tier sites. It concerns crawlers that combine search indexing with model-training and agent use, on pages that carry advertising. Source: src-004, published 2026-07-01.

approved_jobs.statement: When a small team wants code and data to run close to users without managing servers, help them decide what belongs at the edge and what belongs in a region.
CONTROL: When a small operator's business-critical system fails during peak hours in an operational domain unrelated to web infrastructure, help them restore service with limited in-house expertise.

material_constraints.text: Must keep traditional search indexing working while restricting training and agent crawlers
Directive-based blocking is unreliable; a rising share of automated requests ignore it
No dedicated security or platform staff; must be low-operations
Must not break WebSocket, gRPC or other dynamic and API traffic
Predictable flat billing preferred over per-request usage billing
Cannot install a persistent client on ephemeral build compute or unmanaged devices
Cloud-specific certifications and data-residency evidence may block procurement
Cannot afford to duplicate every system to survive one provider's failure
Packaging and process change materially at a 50-user threshold
Non-text and media-heavy workloads may force a tier or vendor change
